author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Rename PS2 working images while preserving serial and set identity
summary: Create a reversible filename map, rename only verified working copies, update cue references and multidisc labels, refresh once, and prove that EmuCoreX still links the correct region and per-game profile.
heroAlt: ImgBurn disc-information screen illustrating source labels and image identity before a working-file rename

blocks.text: A display title and a disc identity are not the same thing

EmuCoreX may derive presentation metadata from the image serial rather than its filename, but storage providers, user backups, cue sheets, and multidisc organization still depend on names. Rename only a playable working copy. Preserve the untouched master and a mapping from old relative path to new relative path, SHA-256, serial, region, revision, and disc number.
Never batch-rename cue/bin sets as independent files. The FILE lines inside the cue sheet must exactly match the renamed track files, including case on case-sensitive storage.

items: A verified hash for every file being renamed.
The detected game serial and region recorded before the change.
A complete list of cue/bin and multidisc relationships.
A backup of per-game profiles and a screenshot of favorites for the test group.
An untouched preservation master outside the working library.

blocks.text: Rename one identity class at a time

items: 1. Choose one single-file DVD image and record its old path, proposed name, hash, serial, and region.
2. Close EmuCoreX, rename that working file with Android's provider or on a computer while the storage is unmounted from Android.
3. Reopen EmuCoreX, refresh once, and confirm the entry still reports the recorded serial and region.
4. Launch the title, inspect its per-game settings, and confirm favorites or recent state remain associated as expected.
5. For a cue/bin set, copy the set to a working folder, rename tracks, update each cue FILE entry, and validate references before scanning it.
6. For multidisc games, use one base title plus explicit Disc 1, Disc 2, and region labels; never rely on alphabetical accidents.
7. Complete the ledger row only after a cold boot and hash verification, then continue with the next small batch.

blocks.text: If EmuCoreX creates a new entry rather than updating the old one, treat it as an identity migration. Compare serial and hash before reapplying a profile. Do not copy a profile from one regional executable merely because the marketing title matches.
Prove names changed but bytes did not
The rename passes only when the working content remains byte-identical and every relationship can be reconstructed from the ledger.

items: Post-rename SHA-256 equals the pre-rename value.
Detected serial, region, and revision remain correct.
Every cue FILE reference resolves to an existing track.
Multidisc order is explicit in both filenames and notes.
The selected game's profile and favorite point at the intended entry.
CD data boots but music is absent: the cue no longer references all audio tracks.
Two discs sort in the wrong order: disc labels are ambiguous.
A new regional entry receives old settings: profile association was assumed rather than verified.
Provider reports success but file is missing after reboot: the rename occurred in a transient or cloud-backed location.

blocks.text: Use the ledger to restore exact paths

Close EmuCoreX and restore original working filenames from the old-to-new map. For cue/bin sets, restore the entire set from the working backup instead of reversing individual lines by memory. Refresh once and verify the original serial, profile, and launch before attempting a smaller rename batch.
Filename characters travel poorly between filesystems

Avoid trailing dots or spaces, reserved Windows characters, and names that differ only by case when a library may move between Android, Windows, Linux, or removable media. A conservative title, region, serial, revision, and disc-number convention is more portable than decorative punctuation.
